headline: Transformation charges obscure underlying profit growth
summary_short: Revenue rose 7.6% year over year to $22.8 billion, but GAAP diluted EPS fell 53% to $0.71 on $1.17 billion of transformation charges, even as non-GAAP adjusted diluted EPS still rose to $1.76.
summary_long: Revenue grew 7.6% y/y to $22.8 billion, led by U.S. Domestic (+6.0%) and International (+12.5%) segment growth on higher revenue per piece. GAAP operating profit fell 48.9% y/y to $930 million and diluted EPS fell 53% to $0.71, driven almost entirely by $1.17 billion of after-tax transformation charges (mainly Driver Choice Program severance) versus $74 million a year ago. Excluding those charges, non-GAAP adjusted operating profit rose to $2.1 billion (+12.0% y/y) and adjusted diluted EPS rose to $1.76 (+13.5% y/y). UPS raised full-year guidance: revenue to approximately $91.2 billion, adjusted operating profit to approximately $8.65 billion, and adjusted diluted EPS to approximately $7.22. Cash was $4.65 billion, down from $5.80 billion at Q1-end.

drivers.explanation: U.S. Domestic revenue rose 6.0% on a 9.3% increase in revenue per piece; International revenue rose 12.5% on an 18.9% increase in revenue per piece.
GAAP operating profit fell mainly on $1.17 billion of transformation strategy costs, chiefly Driver Choice Program severance, versus $74 million a year ago.
Net income fell primarily on after-tax transformation charges of $891 million, or $1.05 per diluted share, mostly employee separation costs from the completed Driver Choice Program.
The $1.05 per-share after-tax transformation charge accounts for most of the EPS decline; excluding it, non-GAAP adjusted diluted EPS rose to $1.76.

Excluding transformation charges, non-GAAP adjusted operating profit rose 12.0% y/y and adjusted diluted EPS rose 13.5%; UPS raised full-year revenue, adjusted operating profit, and adjusted EPS guidance.
